newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan buys 108,000 tonnes U.S. corn at tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys 108,000 tonnes U.S. corn at tender.

text.p: Taiwan's CK group bought two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. No.2 corn from Japan's Mitsui and Co Ltd at a tender on Tuesday, traders said.
The CK Group comprises Chia Hsin Flour Feed and Vegetable Oil Corp and some buyers from Taiwan's southern port city of Kaohsiung.
CK Group's tender was open to corn of Argentine origin but no Argentine bids came in at acceptable prices, traders said.

The lowest Argentine bid was US$146.16 cost-and-freight per tonne from Granac, cheaper than Mitsui's bid but too high for non-U.S. grain, which is seen in Taiwan as more expensive to process, traders said.

Traders say CK Group and other Taiwan corn buyers, which generally prefer U.S. grain, have taken a new interest in relatively cheap Argentine corn for April and May shipments due to a recent rally in U.S. corn futures.
"The recent rise of U.S. corn prices made Argentine corn more attractive to Taiwan buyers," a trader said.
Taiwan buyers would consider buying Argentine corn if the price were US$10 or more below the U.S. corn price, he said.
Both shipments purchased on Tuesday were fixed on an FOB basis with freight costs fixed with MIT, traders said.
The first shipment's freight was fixed at US$14.28 per tonne and the second was at US$14.19 per tonne, both from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, they said.
